newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PARCELLS SIGNS CONTRACT, TAGLIABUE TO HOLD MEETING NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-PARCELLS SIGNS CONTRACT, TAGLIABUE TO HOLD MEETING NEXT WEEK.

text.p: Former New England Patriots head coach Bill Parcells signed a contract with the New York Jets Friday with a meeting looming next week for the NFL commissioner to settle the Patriots-Jets dispute over him.

The six-year contract at undisclosed financial terms commits Parcells, who won two National Football League championships with the New York Giants and took the Patriots to the Super Bowl last month, to coach the Jets for at least four of the six years.

NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue ruled last week that Parcells is contractually bound to the Patriots and could not serve as an NFL head coach or in a comparable position in 1997 without New England's consent.

But the Jets named Parcells as a consultant and Bill Belichick head coach for the 1997 season with the understanding that Parcells will become head coach and chief of football operations in February 1998. The Jets insist that Parcells' consulting role does not violate Tagliabue's ruling.
Tagliabue said Thursday he will convene a meeting that will include Patriots owner Robert Kraft, Jets president Steve Gutman and representatives of Parcells.

The meeting could determine if Parcells' agreement to become a Jets consultant violates his old pact with New England, but it could also give Tagliabue a chance to work out a deal between the clubs. However, Tagliabue hopes a deal can be reached that would make the meeting unnecessary.
The contract signed Friday also contains an option for a seventh year if Parcells serves as a consultant in 1997.
"It's an employment agreement and consulting agreement that we've agreed upon and there's no problem with the league," Gutman said.

"At least four of the years of his employment agreement he will serve as head coach and for all six of those years he will serve as chief football operations officer. He may serve as head coach for the entire period.

"We had said the other day in our earlier conversations that Bill had contemplated only guaranteeing two years on the sideline as head coach," he added. "We were working things through at that time. We have a four-year commitment now."
"I'm going to coach a minimum of four and hopefully more, we'll see," Parcells said.
Parcells said he does not expect to attend next week's meeting.

"I've always been a league guy, I'll abide by whatever the league says. I've done so to this point and I'll continue to do it. If they say I can't do anything for a while, I'm not doing anything for a while," he said.
"I know I'm going to be here in 1998, I know that. I just signed a deal to do that. As of February 1, 1998, I'm going to be here and I'm going to be here for an extended period of time, God willing."

The Patriots have sought compensation for losing Parcells, with the prize plum the top overall pick in the draft the Jets earned with their league-worst season last year. But the Jets say adamantly they will not part with the number one pick, leaving the door open for other picks, players or money.
New England officials have denied reports that the Jets offered two second-round picks as compensation.
Gutman said the Jets already have advised the league that Parcells will not have any game-day role or perform any other "co-head coach" function during the 1997 season.

Kraft has called the Jets' hiring of Parcells as a consultant for 1997 and head coach the following season "a transparent farce." The Patriots formally asked Tagliabue to review the Jets' agreements with Parcells and Belichick on Wednesday.
Belichick, the Patriots' defensive coordinator under Parcells, was signed to a multi-year contract at undisclosed terms and would become the assistant head coach when Parcells takes over.
